--- select_interval_values_with_int64_expr.sql
SELECT
  -- The value of an interval literal is any INT64 expression.
  TIMESTAMP_SUB(ts, INTERVAL 30 DAY),
  TIMESTAMP_SUB(ts, INTERVAL -30 DAY),
  TIMESTAMP_SUB(ts, INTERVAL @n DAY),
  TIMESTAMP_SUB(ts, INTERVAL total_logins DAY),
  TIMESTAMP_SUB(ts, INTERVAL (total_logins) DAY),
  TIMESTAMP_SUB(ts, INTERVAL total_logins * 7 DAY),
  TIMESTAMP_SUB(ts, INTERVAL 7 * 4 DAY),
  TIMESTAMP_SUB(ts, INTERVAL CAST(total_logins AS INT64) DAY),
  TIMESTAMP_SUB(ts, INTERVAL CAST(@n AS INT64) DAY),
  TIMESTAMP_SUB(ts, INTERVAL (SELECT 30) DAY),
  TIMESTAMP_SUB(ts, INTERVAL '3' DAY),

--- SQL
SELECT TIMESTAMP_SUB(ts, INTERVAL 30 DAY), TIMESTAMP_SUB(ts, INTERVAL -30 DAY), TIMESTAMP_SUB(ts, INTERVAL @n DAY), TIMESTAMP_SUB(ts, INTERVAL total_logins DAY), TIMESTAMP_SUB(ts, INTERVAL (total_logins) DAY), TIMESTAMP_SUB(ts, INTERVAL total_logins * 7 DAY), TIMESTAMP_SUB(ts, INTERVAL 7 * 4 DAY), TIMESTAMP_SUB(ts, INTERVAL CAST(total_logins AS INT64) DAY), TIMESTAMP_SUB(ts, INTERVAL CAST(@n AS INT64) DAY), TIMESTAMP_SUB(ts, INTERVAL (SELECT 30) DAY), TIMESTAMP_SUB(ts, INTERVAL "3" DAY)
